Broadacre / Soil testing
Paddock questions

Check the panel. Plan the job.

Use your soil report to talk through what the paddock needs and what’s worth doing this season.

What’s included in the test?

Here’s what one Hybrid-Ag report covered. Use it when comparing quotes and confirm which tests and lab methods you need for your paddock.

Exchange capacityCEC / TEC, base saturation, Hydrogen percentage and Calcium to Magnesium ratio.
Major Elements and saltsCalcium, Magnesium, Potassium, Sodium, Chloride and Sulphur.
Soil conditionpH in water, electrical conductivity (EC) and organic Carbon.
Nitrogen and PhosphorusNitrate and Ammonium Nitrogen. Colwell Phosphorus and Total Phosphorus reported separately.
Other ElementsBoron, Iron, Manganese, Copper, Zinc and Aluminium.
Soil solutionSolution EC, Calcium, Magnesium, Potassium and Sodium.

Questions to ask about your paddock

  • What are we trying to explain in this paddock? Which areas and depths should we sample separately?
  • Where does the test show a Nutrient shortfall in kg/ha, and how much is worth tackling this season?
  • How many kg/ha of that Nutrient are we already putting out, and how much more would the proposed blend supply?
  • Where and when could we place the blend with the gear you’ve got? What would it cost per hectare, and when should we check the result?

Talk it through with Jimmy or Bruce

If you’d like to go through these questions for your paddock, have your soil report handy and ask for Jimmy or Bruce when you get in touch. You can also ask for webinar details once the date is set.

The targets and rounded kg/ha figures apply to this sample. How much to tackle this season is a separate decision.

What goes in the blend?

This sample is short of Calcium and Sulphur. We’d first check what your planned inputs already cover. If the crop needs both this season and liquid placement suits your gear, Liqui-Gyp is one option we’d assess. We’d then work out what the proposed blend supplies in kg/ha.

What do you get back from a soil test?

Conventional and Hybrid-Ag soil testing approaches
CompareConventional approachThe Hybrid-Ag approach
AnalysisConventional approachWhat gets tested depends on the package your supplier offers. Some cover only the basics.The Hybrid-Ag approachWe start with a comprehensive soil panel, then tailor the testing to what you’re seeing in the paddock. If roots stop at a particular depth, for example, we can test the layers separately to see what a topsoil sample might miss.
InterpretationConventional approachA basic report gives you raw readings, sometimes with a low-to-high “fuel gauge”. It flags a shortage without telling you how many kg/ha you’re short.The Hybrid-Ag approachWe calculate the shortfall in kg/ha for each relevant Nutrient and show the soil target behind it. You can see what needs correcting before choosing a blend.
Paddock planConventional approachA recommendation may stop at a paddock rate for gypsum, dolomite or lime. How that fits the rest of the program can be left to you.The Hybrid-Ag approachWe draw on inputs from a range of suppliers to build a Hybrid-Ag prescription blend. We compare liquid and dry options, including granules, against your gear, placement, timing and cost per hectare.

Next time you test Go back to the same zones and depths at a similar time, using comparable lab methods. Look at what changed alongside what went out and how each patch yielded.
